cards.front: What is the difference between association and aggregation?
cards.back: Association is any relationship between two classes; aggregation is a whole-part form of it (HAS-A)
cards.extra: A Driver is associated with Cars; a Car aggregates an Engine. Aggregation says the part belongs to the whole conceptually but can exist independently.

cards.back: A relationship where one class knows about the other but not vice versa
cards.extra: Driver holds a list of Car, while Car has no field pointing back — one arrow, one direction of knowledge.

cards.front: What is the difference between AWT and Swing?
cards.back: AWT is platform-dependent (native peers); Swing is lightweight, drawn by Java, and portable
cards.extra: AWT came first with heavier OS widgets; Swing components start with J and look the same everywhere.

cards.front: What is the difference between StringBuffer and StringBuilder?
cards.back: StringBuffer is synchronized; StringBuilder is not — and therefore faster
cards.extra: Same API. Use StringBuilder unless the builder is genuinely shared between threads, which is rare.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: Why is StringBuilder preferred to String concatenation in a loop?
cards.back: String is immutable, so each += creates a new object; StringBuilder appends in place
cards.extra: The compiler turns a single expression into a builder, but a loop that reassigns a String still allocates per iteration.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.back: A parameter declared Type... that accepts zero or more arguments, packed into an array
cards.extra: It must be the last parameter. Each call allocates an array, so it is not free.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.back: They perform the operation but throw ArithmeticException on overflow, instead of silently wrapping
cards.extra: Java's + on ints wraps around silently. When an overflow must be detected, these are the correct methods.

cards.back: An uncaught exception travels up the call stack until some method catches it or the thread dies
cards.extra: Each frame is popped in turn; if nothing handles it, the default handler prints the stack trace and terminates the thread.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::01 Exception Handling

cards.front: What are the headline features added in Java 8?
cards.back: Lambdas, the Stream API, default and static interface methods, Optional, and the new date-time API
cards.extra: It remains the most disruptive single release: it changed how Java code is written, not just what the library offers.

cards.front: What did Java 9 add that changed everyday code?
cards.back: The module system, factory methods for immutable collections (List.of), private interface methods, and JShell
cards.extra: Modules matter for library authors; the collection factories matter for everyone.

cards.front: What is a servlet, and where does it run?
cards.back: A Java class that extends a web server — it runs inside a servlet container on the server, handling HTTP requests
cards.extra: The container manages its life cycle and converts requests into Java objects. Servlet + JSP was the standard Java web stack before Spring.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::09 Build and Frameworks::06 Web Frameworks
